flow.costPlain: Running Snowflake's platform — data centers and the cost of delivering its product and services.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Sales teams and marketing. Up 25% YoY — growing, but slower than revenue.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Building the platform and its AI products. Up 12% YoY; includes $242M of stock-based pay.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: The back office — finance, legal and admin. Up 22% YoY.

follow100Note: Snowflake spent $129.71 of every $100 it took in on direct and running costs — more than it earned — and other income covered only $3.70 of the gap, leaving a $26.02 loss per $100. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Snowflake reports in thousands (revenue was $1,144,969K); figures here are shown in $M to three decimals so the lines foot exactly. Excluding stock-based pay and other non-GAAP items, operating income was $128M (an 11% margin). Chart note: Snowflake's running costs exceeded its gross profit by $340M and other income covered $42M of that, so the chart draws the remaining $298M net loss as a 'Covered by cash on hand' source, which also covers the $0.06M tax bill.
oneTimers: A $2.1M impairment charge for exiting Snowflake's San Mateo office — part of a $108.6M charge for the first half of FY26, mostly booked in Q1 — excluded from non-GAAP results along with stock-based pay and other items.
otherDetail: Other income of $42M, net: $49M of interest income on Snowflake's cash and investments, less $2M of interest expense and $5M of other expense, net. Net loss attributable to Snowflake Inc. was $298M (EPS -$0.89), after $0.1M of income attributable to noncontrolling interests.

segments.name: Product
segments.note: Customers pay to store data and run computing and AI workloads on Snowflake's platform, billed by how much they use. Up 32% YoY and 95% of all revenue.

segments.name: Professional services and other
segments.note: Help getting set up and moving data onto Snowflake, plus other small items. Up 38% YoY — but it costs more to deliver than it brings in (a $15.0M gross loss).

takeaways.text: Product revenue rose 32% to $1.09B, the net revenue retention rate was 125%, and remaining performance obligations — work customers have already contracted — grew 33% to $6.9B. Snowflake also guided Q3 product revenue to $1,125–$1,130M, up 25–26%.
takeaways.title: Product growth stayed above 30%

takeaways.text: The GAAP operating loss was $340M. The main reason: $436M of stock-based compensation-related charges counted as costs this quarter. Leaving those and similar items out, non-GAAP operating income was $128M, an 11% margin.
takeaways.title: Still a GAAP loss, mostly stock pay

takeaways.text: Snowflake ended the quarter with 654 customers spending over $1M a year on the platform (+30% YoY) and 751 Forbes Global 2000 customers. Operating cash flow was $75M and adjusted free cash flow was $68M.
takeaways.title: Big customers kept spending

verdict: Snowflake's revenue grew 32% to $1.14B, with product revenue up 32% to $1.09B — but $436M of stock-based pay helped leave a GAAP operating loss of $340M and a net loss of $298M.
